entries.headline: Ansible CLAUDE.md still tells slices to target an undeclared repo as ../scratch/<Repo>; the dev plugin's github:<owner>/<repo> Target now clones it
body: Ansible/CLAUDE.md § Related repos: a repo a slice changes but the environment does not declare goes under /work/scratch/<Repo>, and 'its phases say Target: ../scratch/<Repo>, and the environment that runs the slice clones it there first'. The dev plugin (0.9.60, docs/plan-template.md and docs/run-loop.md § The plan is the queue) has a Target: github:<owner>/<repo> form for exactly this case: the driver clones or adopts /work/scratch/<repo> itself, and the dry run does it at planning time. Slice 033's plan uses github:pvginkel/KubeCoder, so it departs from the project's written convention while following the plugin's. The CLAUDE.md sentence does not mention the github: form, so the next plan writer reading it first is steered to the manual-clone form.
entries.consequence: A plan writer following CLAUDE.md writes ../scratch/<Repo> and the run depends on someone having cloned the repo by hand first

Criteria owed after that push — the run cannot prove them, so they stay open until the push lands and are settled after it:

text: What the conversion took, for the verdict (KubeCoder 30df8e2d): Declarative refuses a method call on an object outside script{} ("Method calls on objects not allowed outside \"script\" blocks"), so each of the eight library calls (seven helmCharts.kaniko, one cicd.writeVersionPins) sits in its own script{}; the pin stage's local String needs one too. Keeping the 'Cloning repo' stage takes options{ skipDefaultCheckout() }. GOFLAGS moved from withEnv to stage environment{}. The file grew from 341 to 408 lines, all structure (steps{}/script{} wrappers); no stage, sh step or kaniko destination changed. The linter validates agent parameter names and trigger symbols but does not load the library, so podYaml's call and the library step ahead of pipeline{} are proven only by the Replay.
Count in the note above corrected: nine library calls, each in its own script{} — eight helmCharts.kaniko (one per image stage) and one cicd.writeVersionPins.

entries.headline: JenkinsPipelineUtils cicd.applyPins writes a pin into a sequence entry's mapping instead of refusing the path
body:
applyPins skips a sequence entry's own line (`  - name: LOG_LEVEL`), but the entry's later keys (`    value: info`) match its `key: ...` pattern and take the enclosing mapping's path. So in `env:
  - name: LOG_LEVEL
    value: info
` the pin `env.value` resolves and is written (`value: debug`) where its doc comment promises a throw: 'A path that does not resolve to exactly one scalar line throws … neither may reach a commit.' With two such entries the pin is refused as 'on both line …', which names the wrong cause. VersionPinsTest asserts only the entry's first key (`env.name`) is refused and pins nothing about later keys. A fix tracks an open sequence entry like the open block scalar (`literal`), so keys under it carry no path.
entries.consequence: A Jenkinsfile that names a pin path running through a YAML list gets that list entry's value overwritten in the deploy repo and committed, with no error, instead of a refused build
entries.author:
code-writer, P1, r1: a throwaway JUnit probe calling applyPins('f', 'env:
 - name: LOG_LEVEL
 value: info
', [env.value: debug]) returned the file with 'value: debug'

entries.headline: JenkinsPipelineUtils cicd.normalizePins is not asserted: its String keys and its refusal of a values file named twice
body: normalizePins (vars/cicd.groovy) is @NonCPS and pure, like the three functions VersionPinsTest covers, but R2's list did not name it and P1 left it out. It turns GString keys and values into Strings (a GString key is unreadable by subscript) and throws 'pins names <file> twice' when a String and a GString spell the same values file. A test in VersionPinsTest, reached the same way, would pin both.
entries.consequence: A change that drops the refusal or the String conversion keeps the gate green; the build then writes only one of the two pin sets for that file, or none, and deploys the previous image without an error
entries.author: code-writer, P1, r1: vars/cicd.groovy normalizePins against tests/…/VersionPinsTest.java

entries.headline: JenkinsPipelineUtils test-gate comments (tests/pom.xml, .kubecoder/project.yaml) say every @NonCPS function has behaviour tests; normalizePins and rebuildAtIso have none
body: tests/pom.xml:5-6 says the gate 'asserts the behaviour of its @NonCPS functions', and .kubecoder/project.yaml:13 says 'asserts the behaviour of the @NonCPS functions'. cicd.normalizePins (vars/cicd.groovy:155) and helmCharts.rebuildAtIso (vars/helmCharts.groovy:202) are @NonCPS, and no test under tests/src calls either one. The normalizePins gap itself is T1.
entries.consequence: A maintainer who trusts the comment can change normalizePins or rebuildAtIso, see the gate stay green, and take the change as covered when no test checks it

entries.headline: DesignAssistant's Jenkinsfiles still call containerTemplates.canon, which JenkinsPipelineUtils P2 deleted
body: P2 deleted `containerTemplates.canon` on the plan's grounding that it had no caller in any `Jenkinsfile*` under /work and /work/scratch. `pvginkel/DesignAssistant` is not cloned in this environment, and on GitHub it still calls the helper: `Jenkinsfile:13` (main and develop) and `Jenkinsfile.deploy-uat:13` (main and develop) build their pod with `containerTemplates.canon('canon')`. No live job runs these files. The controller's job tree has no DesignAssistant or Archived folder (read 2026-09-30), and the removed jobs' configs are saved under /work/scratch/jenkins-config/xml-deleted/Archived/DesignAssistant/ (Build-Main, Build-Develop, Deploy-UAT, Deploy-PRD). If Build-Main, Build-Develop or Deploy-UAT is restored from that config, it fails when it builds its pod template. Deploy-PRD calls only containerTemplates.k8s.
entries.consequence: If the DesignAssistant jobs are restored from their saved config, Build-Main, Build-Develop and Deploy-UAT fail on every build with a missing-method error for containerTemplates.canon until the Jenkinsfiles or the library change
entries.author: code reviewer, P2, round 1, phases/P2/code_review_r1.md F1

entries.headline: JenkinsPipelineUtils: the k8s and modern-app-toolchain sidecar settings are written twice, in containerTemplates and in podYaml.sidecars()
body: Ruling F1 leaves containerTemplates untouched, so podYaml carries its own copy of the two sidecars' settings: registry:5000/k8s:1.35.5 and registry:5000/kube-coder-modern-app-toolchain:node-24 with uid 1000 (vars/podYaml.groovy sidecars(), vars/containerTemplates.groovy k8s/modern_app_toolchain). A comment on sidecars() names the pairing; no test compares them. If the verdict keeps scripted pod pipelines, both stay, and one source (or a test that both agree) removes the chance of a bump landing in one only. If the verdict migrates everything, the describables go and so does the duplicate.
entries.consequence: A sidecar image bump made in containerTemplates alone leaves KubeCoder's declarative build on the old image, with no error.
entries.author: code-writer, P3, r1, vars/podYaml.groovy

entries.headline: JenkinsPipelineUtils podYaml names a string images: entry after its last path segment even when that is not a valid Kubernetes container name
body: containerName (vars/podYaml.groovy:124-126) strips path and tag and passes the rest through. Image repository names may hold '.' and '_', which RFC 1123 container names may not: a probe rendered name "my_tool" for registry:5000/my_tool:1 and name "tool.v2" for ghcr.io/foo/tool.v2. podYaml accepts the call; the failure comes when the pod template is built or the API server refuses the pod, and the caller must use the map form with an explicit name. No image in this slice (P4's k8s, modern-app-toolchain, golang, node) is affected.
entries.consequence: A pipeline that passes such an image as a string gets a build that fails at pod creation until it switches to the map form with a name:
entries.author: code-reviewer, P3, round 1, phases/P3/code_review_r1.md F1

entries.headline: JenkinsPipelineUtils podYaml renders an env value of null as the string "null"
body: imageContainer converts env values with value.toString() (vars/podYaml.groovy:113); Groovy's null.toString() is "null". A probe rendered env: [A: null] as value: "null". A pipeline passing an unset variable or parameter as an env value gets the literal text null in the container, with no refusal.
entries.consequence: A container started with an env value from an unset variable sees the literal string null and acts on it, with no error at build start
entries.author: code-reviewer, P3, round 1, phases/P3/code_review_r1.md F2

entries.headline: Delete the scratch clone /work/scratch/KubeCoder once the slice is done
body: The driver cloned (or adopted) `/work/scratch/KubeCoder` for `Target: github:pvginkel/KubeCoder`; the slice's phases for that repo are branched, merged and pushed there.

Deleting it is safe once the slice's commits are on origin — the push check before the doc phase confirms that. A clone left in place is synced by every later preflight in this environment and adopted by the next `github:` target naming that repo.
entries.consequence: none in this run — the clone is where the run works; left behind, it only takes disk space and a sync in every later preflight.
entries.author: the driver's target resolution

entries.headline: KubeCoder docs/operations/pipeline-dependencies.md still describes Build-Main's pod as the scripted podTemplate with golang/node containerTemplates
body: The Build and deploy table (lines 16-17) cites `Jenkinsfile`'s `podTemplate` (`containerTemplates.k8s`, `containerTemplates.modern_app_toolchain`) and the `golang` `containerTemplate`, and the Pinned toolchains table (line 40) cites the `node` `containerTemplate`. After P4 (KubeCoder 30df8e2d) the Jenkinsfile is declarative: `agent { kubernetes { inheritFrom 'jenkins-agent kaniko'; yamlMergeStrategy merge(); yaml podYaml(templates: ['k8s', 'modern-app-toolchain'], images: [[image: …go-toolchain…, name: 'golang', …], 'node:24-bookworm']) } }`. P4's done-record left this for the doc phase. The file is not in the slice's diff, and the KubeCoder change is under a push hold until the operator's Replay.
entries.consequence: A reader looking for where Build-Main's sidecars and toolchain images are pinned is sent to podTemplate/containerTemplate calls the Jenkinsfile no longer has
